footer.text: MVP - Derivative Simulator for Retail Customers

pathDependency.explText1: The certificate reacts to daily changes.
pathDependency.dragWarning2: shows the impact of path dependency.
pathDependency.dragWarning3: With high volatility, this can lead to significant losses!

explanation.warrantCall: You are betting on rising prices. If the underlying is above {{strike}} EUR at maturity, you receive the difference multiplied by the subscription ratio. Your break-even is at {{breakeven}} EUR. Below that, the warrant expires worthless.
explanation.warrantPut: You are betting on falling prices. If the underlying is below {{strike}} EUR at maturity, you receive the difference multiplied by the subscription ratio. Your break-even is at {{breakeven}} EUR. Above that, the warrant expires worthless.
explanation.knockoutCall: Knock-Out Long: You profit from rising prices with constant leverage.
explanation.knockoutCallWarning: Warning: If the underlying falls to or below {{barrier}} EUR, the product expires worthless immediately!
explanation.knockoutPut: Knock-Out Short: You profit from falling prices with constant leverage.
explanation.knockoutPutWarning: Warning: If the underlying rises to or above {{barrier}} EUR, the product expires worthless immediately!
explanation.knockoutBarrierType: Important: Check whether your product has a continuous barrier (monitored intraday) or a discrete barrier (checked only at specific times, e.g., end of day). This significantly affects knock-out risk!
explanation.factor: Factor {{factor}}x {{direction}}: The certificate reflects the daily percentage change of the underlying with factor {{factor}}.
explanation.factorCallExample: If the underlying rises by 1%, the certificate gains {{factor}}%.
explanation.factorPutExample: If the underlying falls by 1%, the certificate gains {{factor}}%.
explanation.factorWarning: Warning: Path dependency! With longer holding periods, performance can deviate significantly from the expected result.

info.currentPrice: The current market price of the underlying asset (e.g., stock, index). This is the reference point for all calculations. Changes in this price directly affect the value of your derivative.
info.strikePrice: The strike price is the price at which you can buy (Call) or sell (Put) the underlying. It determines whether the option is in, at, or out of the money. For Knock-Outs, it's the base price for calculating the certificate value.
info.impliedVol: Implied volatility reflects the market's expectation of future price fluctuations. Higher volatility increases option prices as larger price swings become more likely. It's expressed as annualized percentage.
info.maturity: The remaining time until expiration. Longer maturity means more time value, but also more time decay (Theta). Options lose value as expiration approaches, especially in the last weeks.
info.drift: The expected annual return of the underlying asset. Used in Monte Carlo simulations to model future price paths. A positive drift means prices are expected to rise on average.
info.riskFree: The risk-free interest rate (e.g., government bond yield). Used in Black-Scholes pricing. Higher rates increase Call values and decrease Put values slightly.
info.ratio: The subscription ratio determines how many units of the underlying one derivative represents. A ratio of 0.1 means you need 10 warrants to control 1 unit of the underlying.
info.knockoutBarrier: The price level at which the Knock-Out certificate expires worthless immediately. For Calls, it's below the current price; for Puts, above. Closer barriers mean higher leverage but more risk.
info.factor: The leverage factor multiplies daily percentage changes. A 3x factor means if the underlying moves 1%, the certificate moves 3%. Works in both directions!
info.adjustmentThreshold: The adjustment threshold prevents a total loss on very large adverse moves. If the underlying moves against the position by this threshold or more within a day, an intraday reset is applied (the day is split into segments). This can reduce the loss but still leads to significant drawdowns.
info.warrant: A warrant is a leveraged derivative that gives you the right (but not the obligation) to buy (Call) or sell (Put) an underlying asset at a specific price (strike) until a certain date. The value is determined by intrinsic value and time value.
info.knockout: A Knock-Out certificate offers leveraged exposure to the underlying. The price is calculated using barrier option theory (closed-form Rubinstein-Reiner formula), which considers the probability of hitting the barrier. If the underlying reaches the barrier, the product expires worthless immediately.
info.factor: A Factor certificate multiplies the daily percentage change of the underlying by a fixed factor. Due to path dependency, the long-term performance can deviate significantly from the expected leveraged return.
info.volatilityAnn: Annualized volatility of the underlying used for the scenario path. A value like 30% p.a. means typical daily moves are around 30% / sqrt(252).
info.timeHorizon: Simulation time horizon in trading days used for the path dependency chart. Factor certificates are open-end, so this is not a maturity.
info.status: Shows whether the option is In the Money (ITM), At the Money (ATM), or Out of the Money (OTM). ITM means the option has intrinsic value, OTM means it would expire worthless if exercised now.
info.intrinsicValue: The intrinsic value is the immediate exercise value of the option. For a Call: max(0, Underlying - Strike). For a Put: max(0, Strike - Underlying). It can never be negative.
info.timeValue: The time value represents the probability that the option will gain more value before expiration. It depends on remaining time, volatility, and distance to strike. Time value decays as expiration approaches (Theta).
info.breakeven: The break-even point is the price at which you neither profit nor lose. For a Call: Strike + Premium. For a Put: Strike - Premium. Above/below this point, you start making profit.
info.leverage: Leverage shows how much stronger the derivative moves compared to the underlying. A leverage of 5x means a 1% move in the underlying results in approximately 5% move in the derivative.
info.bsPrice: The Black-Scholes price is the theoretical fair value of the option, calculated using the Black-Scholes model. It considers underlying price, strike, time to maturity, volatility, and risk-free rate.
info.delta: Delta measures how much the option price changes for a 1 EUR move in the underlying. Delta of 0.5 means the option moves 0.50 EUR for every 1 EUR move. Calls have positive Delta, Puts negative.
info.gamma: Gamma measures how much Delta changes for a 1 EUR move in the underlying. High Gamma means Delta changes quickly, which is typical for at-the-money options near expiration.
info.vega: Vega measures the sensitivity to volatility changes. A Vega of 0.10 means the option price increases by 0.10 EUR if implied volatility rises by 1 percentage point.
info.theta: Theta measures daily time decay. A Theta of -0.05 means the option loses 0.05 EUR per day due to time passing, all else being equal. Theta accelerates near expiration.
info.maxLoss: The maximum loss for buying options is limited to the premium paid. You can never lose more than your initial investment, unlike short positions.
info.koDistance: The distance to the knock-out barrier in percent. The smaller the distance, the higher the risk of knock-out. Watch this closely as markets can move quickly.
info.value: The fair value of the Knock-Out certificate, calculated using closed-form barrier option pricing (Rubinstein-Reiner). It includes both intrinsic value and time value, discounted by the probability of knock-out. This is more accurate than simple intrinsic value.
info.onePlus: Shows the expected percentage change of the certificate when the underlying moves by +1%. For a 3x Long factor certificate, this would be +3%.
